section_title: What does it mean that the Lord opens Lydia’s heart?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 14 Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.

context_lines: The travelers cross from Troas through Samothrace and Neapolis to Philippi, which Luke identifies as a Roman colony. On the Sabbath they go outside the gate to a place of prayer by the river and speak to the women gathered there.

Lydia is a dealer in purple cloth from Thyatira and a worshiper of God. The word behind worshiper comes from **σέβομαι** (*sebomai*, SEH-boh-my), meaning to show deep respect or worship; [Thayer’s entry](https://biblehub.com/greek/4576.htm) includes this verse. Luke says the Lord opens her heart to respond to Paul’s message.

She and her household are baptized, and she urges the travelers to stay in her house. Her response includes hospitality as well as hearing the message. Luke does not describe the ages or relationships of everyone in the household.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians agree that the Lord opens Lydia’s heart as she hears Paul’s message. They explain the relationship between God’s grace and the person’s response in different ways.

The Reformed [Westminster Confession, chapter 10, paragraphs 1–2](https://www.opc.org/wcf.html), teaches that God renews the will and brings those He has chosen to Christ, making them willing so that they come freely. [Calvin on verse 14](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/calvin/acts/16.htm) connects Lydia’s response with that gracious inward work alongside Paul’s spoken message.

The Catholic Church’s [Catechism, paragraphs 153–155](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_one/section_one/chapter_three/article_1/iii_the_characteristics_of_faith.index.html), describes faith as God’s gift and a human act in which the mind and will cooperate with grace. The Methodist [Articles of Religion, Article VIII](https://www.umc.org/en/content/articles-of-religion), likewise teach that grace goes before a person’s good will and works with the response. These readings all recognize God’s initiative while explaining its relation to the response differently.
god_plan_lines: Paul later thanks God for the Philippians’ partnership in the gospel from the first day in [Philippians 1:3–6](https://biblehub.com/bsb/philippians/1.htm). Lydia’s welcome offers a concrete beginning to the shared life surrounding the mission in this city.

[Philippians 4:15–18](https://biblehub.com/bsb/philippians/4.htm) describes the community’s later material support for Paul. That later generosity is not attributed to Lydia alone; it shows how the gospel’s arrival can grow into an ongoing partnership of service and care.
current_position_lines: Worship as the Early Church Knew It directly examines Lydia as a worshiper of God whose heart is opened to hear the message. The study emphasizes reverence, a heart turned toward God, rather than treating worship merely as participation in a ceremony. The account gives the Lord the credit for opening her heart.

deeper_study.title: Worship as the Early Church Knew It

editorial_review.position_source_detail: Worship as the Early Church Knew It — Acts16:14 Lydia’s Heart Was Already in Awe; limited to reverence and the Lord opening her heart, not a new election ruling or an independently verified causal mechanism.
